examples.japanese: {川|かわ}で{石|いし}を{拾|ひろ}った。
examples.english: I picked up stones at the river.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{石|いし}を{集|あつ}めている。
{石|いし}に{躓|つまず}いて{転|ころ}んだ。
examples.english: I tripped on a stone and fell.

examples.japanese: {丸|まる}い{石|いし}を{見|み}つけた。
{石|いし}で{家|いえ}を{建|た}てた。
examples.english: They built a house with stone.

examples.japanese: この{山|やま}には{大|おお}きな{石|いし}がたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many large rocks on this mountain.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}の{道|みち}は{歩|ある}きにくい。
examples.english: Stone paths are difficult to walk on.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{石|いし}を{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: I arranged stones in the garden.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}の{階段|かいだん}を{上|のぼ}った。

notes:
{石|いし} covers both small stones you can pick up and stone as a material. For large boulders or bedrock, {岩|いわ} is used instead.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {石|いし}を{投|な}げる: to throw a stone
- {石|いし}を{拾|ひろ}う: to pick up stones
- {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}: perseverance pays off (lit. three years on a stone)
- {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}: killing two birds with one stone

COMPOUNDS:
- {宝石|ほうせき}: jewel, gem
- {岩石|がんせき}: rock (scientific/geological)
- {石橋|いしばし}: stone bridge
- {石垣|いしがき}: stone wall
- {化石|かせき}: fossil

CONTRAST:
- {石|いし}: stone or rock (general, any size up to what you might carry)
- {岩|いわ}: boulder, large rock, bedrock (too large to move easily)
